notes.claim: A prefix attached to a unit symbol forms a new inseparable symbol that can be raised to a positive or negative power.
Converting between metric units of area and volume means multiplying or dividing by the factor squared for area and cubed for volume.
Units formed by division can be written with a solidus or with negative exponents, so m/s² is also m · s⁻² (added for i6's fix).
The newton is kg m s⁻², and the pascal, the unit of pressure and stress, is N/m² = kg m⁻¹ s⁻² (added for i6's fix).
Resistivity is measured in ohm metres, Ω m (added for i6's fix).
A conductor's resistance is its resistivity times its length divided by its cross-section area, R = ρL/A (added for i6's fix).
Working units through a formula catches slips: a mass divided by an area gives kg/m², where density must be in kg/m³ (added for i6's fix).

sources.quote: The grouping formed by a prefix symbol attached to a unit symbol constitutes a new inseparable symbol (forming a multiple or submultiple of the unit concerned) which can be raised to a positive or negative power

sources.quote: When converting between metric units of area and volume, the numbers you have to multiply or divide by need to be squared for area and cubed for volume.

sources.title: NIST Guide to the SI, Chapter 6: Rules and Style Conventions for Printing and Using Units | NIST
sources.quote: Symbols for units formed from other units by division are indicated by means of a solidus (oblique stroke, / ) , a horizontal line, or negative exponents.

sources.title: 9.3 Resistivity and Resistance - University Physics Volume 2 | OpenStax
sources.quote: The unit of resistivity in SI units is the ohm-meter .

sources.title: 9.3 Resistivity and Resistance - University Physics Volume 2 | OpenStax
sources.quote: The resistance of a cylindrical segment of a conductor is equal to the resistivity of the material times the length divided by the area

sources.title: Dimensional Analysis – Isaac Science
sources.quote: if you mistakenly divided a mass by an area to get density, the answer would be in kg/ m 2 . Given that we know density must be in kg/ m 3 we would spot the mistake.
